question.problem:
Consider the linear transformation 
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}4x+2y \\ 6x+3y\end{aligned}]$ 
and the vectors 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6\end{aligned}],{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$
Which of the given vectors belong to the kernel of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

Therefore, we need to compute $T({v}_{i})$ for each vector ${v}_{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T({v}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\,T({v}_{2})=0,$ we conclude that the only vector that belongs to the kernel of $\,T$ is ${v}_{2}.$
